judged_text: The diff adds a new authenticated write API endpoint and two new shared OAuth utilities (refreshOAuthTokens, parseRefreshTokenResponse) that alter the token-refresh path of eight integrations, with zero test files or assertions anywhere in the diff (no spec/test/itest-shaped file appears in the changed paths). A regression in the placeholder refresh_token mutation or the raw-Response return type (both present in this diff) would break every booking on the affected integrations and ship undetected; there is no verification of the webhook's auth rejection, schema validation, or create-vs-update branch, and no fixture proving the sync endpoint contract (fetch body shape, response shape) matches what all eight call sites expect.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces verifiable correctness issues beyond “missing tests”. `parseRefreshTokenResponse()` returns a Zod `safeParse` result (`{ success, data, error }`), but at least one call site treats it as the parsed credential object: in `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` is then persisted via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, which would store the wrapper object instead of the credential payload (previously `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` returned the payload). Also, `refreshOAuthTokens()` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` when sync is enabled, but some callers expect a token JSON/object (e.g. `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts` assigns its return to `HubspotToken`), which would break at runtime when the env flags enable the sync path.
